_comment: Project-scope Claude Code settings for this repository, checked in deliberately.
This is the ONE place the kit activates a hook on someone's behalf rather than
printing a registration for them to paste. The conventions section of AGENTS.md
records why, beside the opt-in rule it bends. In short: a user-level registration
does not reach a cloud session, and a cloud session is the exact case this hook
exists for, so there is no other mechanism that works where it is needed.
Scoped as narrowly as the exception allows. One hook, in the reminder shape, which
never blocks and never writes: the worst case is one injected paragraph telling you
something you already knew. It fires only on a genuinely new session, not on resume,
clear, compact, or fork.
The path is repository-relative on purpose. install.py's printed registration uses an
absolute path into the user's home, because that copy is placed there; this one points
at the hook in the checkout, so a fresh clone runs it with nothing installed at all,
which is the state it reports on.
The interpreter is python3, not python, and the choice is load-bearing rather than
stylistic. python3 is the portable default: this file exists to reach CLOUD sessions,
which run on Linux, where many distributions ship no `python` at all, and macOS has not
shipped one since 12.3. The hazard in the other direction is real and observed, not
argued: feat-0038 hit the registered-and-inert failure on Windows, where `python3`
resolved to the Store alias, the hook never launched, nothing was emitted, and the
session proceeded looking exactly as it would if skills were reachable.
This block used to defend that choice with a counterfactual, saying the first draft's
`python` would have failed to launch in the exact environment the exception was granted
for. It closed by noting it was found by independent verification before any cloud run,
which was true and was the tell: the claim had been checked against reasoning, never
against the environment. The first measurement contradicted it. Observation 3 of the
2026-08-21 reachability run, in a cloud container reporting Linux and Python 3.11.15,
found both interpreters present: `command -v python3` returned /usr/local/bin/python3
and `command -v python` returned /usr/local/bin/python. On that platform, on that date,
the first draft would have launched.
That is one container on one day, not a claim about every environment, and the lost
scope is what the old sentence got wrong. python3 stays: it is the choice that survives
the environments nobody here has measured.
A static JSON file cannot probe, so this cannot be right on both platforms at once.
The trade is deliberate: cloud sessions are the reason the file is committed at all,
and a Windows developer who wants the hook locally adds the same block with `python`
to .claude/settings.local.json, which Claude Code does not check in. That is the
platform's own mechanism for a personal override.
Contract for the module: .agents/hooks/README.md
